text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- A new survey shows that in one year one in every eight Danes buys via mail order and mail order companies expect the market to continue growing. The Danish association of mail order companies now has 60 members while the number of small companies outside the association is estimated at 50.

--- A number of deadly blood diseases have appeared in Denmark due to recent years' immigration. The diseases are hereditary but not contagious. About two percent of 400 immigrants carry the diseases in their genes without knowing it.
--- The university of Aalborg in nothern Denmark will open an international research school in January 1997. The university hopes to attract about 30 international researchers.

--- Kurdish restaurant owners living in Denmark who give their restaurants Kurdish names are said to have been threatened by the Turkish embassy in Copenhagen and told to change the names of their restaurants. The embassy denies pressuring the Kurds.

--- A new price war on flights in Scandinavia could bring fares dowm by 20 percent. If prices by 10 percent Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) will have to cut expenses and intensify its collaboration with Lufthansa, experts say.

--- Experts warn foreign companies against investing in Denmark as tax legislation is changed constantly. On an avarage the Danish parliament adopts a new tax law every week which makes tax experts characterise Denmark as an unstable tax country.
